transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can't stop focusing on my face. The left side of it, specifically. It looks really uneven and puffy. 

I see it constantly on video calls for work, and in photos from my salsa dancing group. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see what I'm talking about, but... I do. And it's just getting to the point where it's really starting to mess with my work and my social life, so I figured I needed to talk to someone.
How certain are you that the left side of your face is truly uneven and puffy, despite what other people tell you?

I'm... I'm very certain. I know people say they don't see it, but I look at my face every day. When I'm looking at the screen during a support call, it's just... it's right there. The left side is clearly puffier. I don't really know why my friends or coworkers can't see it, or maybe they're just trying to be polite, but I know what I'm seeing.
Can you consider that the left side of your face might not actually be uneven or puffy, or does that feel impossible to believe?

I mean... I don't really know how to answer that. It feels pretty impossible to believe it's not there. 

When I look at my screen or in the mirror, the puffiness is just... it's right in front of me. So, no, I guess I can't really consider that it might not be real, because I see it with my own eyes every single day.
When you notice the puffiness, do you repeatedly check your face in mirrors, photos, or video screens?

Yes, I do. A lot. Before any work meeting or before I go out with my salsa group, I just... I keep opening the camera preview on my phone or computer. I'll sit there changing the angle, moving the lighting around, trying to fix my hair so it covers that side of my face better. 

If I'm taking pictures, I'll retake them over and over. And I keep asking my friends if I look strange or if the puffiness is obvious. I do it so much that I end up being late, or honestly, I just get so drained from the whole process that I don't even want to go out anymore.
Do you mainly worry that the left side of your face looks unattractive or abnormal, or do you believe it shows that you have a physical disease or medical condition?

No, I don't think it's a disease or anything medical like that. I've never really thought it was a health issue. I just... I worry that it looks weird. Abnormal, like you said. I just think it makes me look unattractive and lopsided, not sick.
Do you believe your friends and coworkers are deliberately pretending not to see the puffiness?

Um, no, I don't think they're deliberately pretending. I mean, I guess they might just be trying to be polite when I ask them, or they just don't want to make me feel bad. But I don't think they're, like, secretly lying to me or anything like that. They probably just don't really know what to say when I keep bringing it up.
